long_biography.plain_text:
Coronet began in 1967 with synthetic linings for shoes, expanding into polyurethane-coated surfaces for leather goods, clothing, furnishings and vehicles. Its founder combined equity control with day-to-day management, and Italian production provided the technical base for overseas factories. The product range progressively moved toward recycled, bio-based and solvent-free polymers.

A 2002 disposal left De Marco as chief executive with a repurchase option. He later brought the business back under family ownership, closed underperforming sites and supported manufacturing capacity in China and Vietnam. After its return to stability, he served as honorary president during the succession to Umberto. The elder De Marco is no longer a director; his disclosed holding has fallen to one per cent as the second generation leads further acquisitions.

uncertainties.detail: Enrico De Marco is a common Italian name. The resolution rests on the unusual combined anchors: Coronet patron and Italian fashion-materials industrialist, a 42-metre Aldebaran yacht in contemporary reporting, the exact L'Aldebaran Primo name and Enrico De Marco business in a maritime employment record, and matching vessel dimensions. No namesake shares that full company, sector and yacht pattern.

Secondary articles imply an approximate 1940 or 1941 birth year and connect De Marco with Trezzano sul Naviglio, but they do not agree closely enough or establish whether Trezzano was his birthplace rather than residence. Birth day, month, year and place remain unproposed.

The evidence establishes that De Marco founded Coronet in 1967 but does not document family capital, inherited business access, an independent start or a materially advantaged platform. Wealth origin is therefore the broad Self-made category, not either starting-position subtype.

Coronet's current report gives De Marco only a 1% stake and excludes him from the board after the transfer to Umberto. Manufacturing is used because this remains his sole transparent current wealth-producing interest, but private investments or holdings outside the company may not be publicly visible.

The 2002 sale and continued chief-executive role are contemporaneously documented, while the 2008 reacquisition and turnaround are described retrospectively by Formiche through earlier Italian business coverage. The biographies retain the durable sell-reacquire-restructure arc but omit price, revenue, loss and production-volume figures.

Forbes-first searches found no dedicated profile. Searches returned several namesake LinkedIn profiles, including a Fincantieri technology executive, but none securely matched the older Coronet founder. Coronet's website is institutional rather than a personal profile, so no social proposal is made.

Chemicals is the minimum useful approved active tag because polyurethane coating, polymer resins and bio-polyols are the defining technology of Coronet's manufacturing business under De Marco. Apparel manufacturing is excluded because Coronet manufactures technical inputs for footwear and fashion companies rather than finished apparel.

The biographies focus on Coronet's founding, industrial model, recovery, Asian production and generational transition. Yacht ownership, guests, friendships, transaction values, net-worth claims and dated operating figures are deliberately excluded.
